   STAFF REPORT
 Meeting Date:  March 6, 2026
 To:  Arts and Culture Council Liaisons Councilmember John Mirisch and
  Councilmember Mary Wells
 From:  Brandy Scott, Arts & Culture Program Associate
 Subject:  Recommendation for the relocation of Home by Charles Arnoldi
 Attachments:  1. Photo montage for proposed installation sites

INTRODUCTION
In 1991 the City purchased and installed the sculpture Home by Charles Arnoldi on the corner of
Rexford Drive and Burton Way just south of the Beverly Hills Public Library (BHPL). The nine foot
tall, 1,400-pound, bronze sculpture was purchased for $72,760, upon approval by then-Fine Art
Commission, City Council, as well as the Charles Moore Renovation Group, the firm responsible
for the 1990 remodel of the BHPL. The sculpture is mounted on a square, poured cement base.

DISCUSSION
During the November 7, 2024, study session, City Council approved a recommendation from the
October 7th Permanent Memorial Ad Hoc Committee, to create a memorial plaza for the victims
of the October 7, 2023, attack in Israel. At the August 19, 2025, City Council Study Session, City
Council approved a design for the memorial site that definitively calls for the necessary removal
and relocation of the Charles Arnoldi Home sculpture. With the design chosen, and need to
relocate Home, staff began looking for alternative installation sites for this important part of the
City’s Fine Art Collection.

During the Arts and Culture Commission Regular Meeting held on December 9, 2025, staff
provided a report seeking a recommendation from the Commission for a new site to relocate the
sculpture. The commission voted unanimously to recommend Coldwater Canyon Park as the
preferred location, desiring to reserve other sites and locations for more preeminent future
acquisitions. The list of potential sites generated through the evaluation process for consideration,
is comprised of city staff locating potential new sites and commission feedback and
recommendations, with the express goal of selecting a site which will offer optimum visibility to
 Meeting Date: March 6, 2026

pedestrian and vehicular traffic, proximity to monitoring systems such as CCTV, and aesthetic
compatibility to the surrounding landscape. The below sites were reviewed by the City Architect
and were presented as viable for consideration by the Arts and Culture Commission.

  1. Beverly Gardens Park - north-west corner of Santa Monica Blvd. / Rexford Dr.
  (recommended by the Recreation and Parks Commission)
  2. Coldwater Canyon Park - 1100 Coldwater Canyon Drive (recommended by the Arts
  and Culture Commission)
  3. La Cienega Tennis Center - 325 S. La Cienega Blvd. #1
  4. La Cienega Tennis Center - 325 S. La Cienega Blvd. #2
  5. Roxbury Memorial Park – 471 Roxbury Drive
  6. Will Rogers Memorial Park - 9650 Sunset Blvd. / Beverly Drive

On January 27, 2026, staff provided a presentation to the Recreation and Parks Commission
including the recommendation of the Arts and Culture Commission to relocate Home to Coldwater
Canyon Park. Staff were seeking the support of the Recreation and Parks Commission for the
potential relocation of Home on public park sites, which would fall under their purview if relocated
to a park location. The Recreation and Parks Commission felt strongly that the Beverly Gardens
site would be a better site due to its higher visibility to the general public in comparison to
Coldwater Canyon Park.
Following this presentation to the Arts and Culture Council Liaisons, staff will return to City Council
to seek full approval of a preferred site for relocation. Staff secured a vendor quote for
deinstallation of the sculpture from its current location, in the amount of $11,300, along with a
potential as-needed monthly storage fee of $180 per month until the sculpture is relocated. The
vendor confirmed that the base would need to be demolished in order to facilitate the deinstall.
Additionally, staff have contacted the artist, who confirmed the base was not integral to the art,
and could be reconstructed at the City’s discretion in design and material.
Staff will work with the Project Administration staff, including the City Architect and engineers, to
determine final costs of a new base build, transport, and installation of the sculpture once a site
has been finalized. The funding for this project is available through the Fine Art Fund, a restricted
fund that can only be used for fine art-related expenses.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff are seeking a recommendation from Arts and Culture Council Liaisons for a new installation
site for the relocation of Home by Charles Arnoldi. Upon receiving a recommendation from City
Council Liaisons, this item will be brought forward to the full City Council for final approval.

  Stephanie Harris,
  Director of Community Services
  Approved By
